newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks extend gains as hotel shares boom.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks extend gains as hotel shares boom.

text.p: Croatian stocks extended their gains on Tuesday, led by advances in hotel shares, but traders said it was unclear how long the market could manage to hold onto its recent advances.
"The interest of the public has boosted share prices, but it is impossible to say whether they will continue to rise, stabilise or fall," said one.

Market participants noted strong demand for shares of hoteliers based on the Istrian peninsula as investors grow increasingly optimistic over prospects for Croatia's tourism industry, the country's main source of hard currency earnings.
Seaside hoteliers -- Laguna Porec, Riviera, Istraturist, Arenaturist and Suncani Hvar -- all touched new record highs after posting strong gains.
Laguna rose 100 kuna to close at 1,100, while Riviera added 75 kuna to 280.

Continuing to rise on expectations of a deal with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, confectioner Kras rose 20 kuna to close at 680 on volume of 1,377 shares. It peaked at a record 719 earlier in the session.
Eight of 10 traded issues rose, one was flat and only food processor Podravka defied the market's trend to close down one kuna at 277 on volume of 2,364 shares.
Zagrebacka Banka, the country's biggest bank, was the day's most active issue, rising 30 kunas to 1,000, just 10 kuna shy of last week's all-time high, on volume of 10,446 shares.
The central bank exchange rate was fixed at 5.4551 kuna to the dollar, easing slightly from 5.4527.
